title: Brigham Young’s long missions end with a charge to his family
setting: Brigham Young left Nauvoo in 1839 for a mission to England with other apostles. His wife, Mary Ann Angell Young, and their children faced poverty and illness while he was gone. Young, Heber Kimball, and John Taylor arrived back in Nauvoo on 1 July 1841. Eight days later, Joseph Smith dictated this revelation at Young’s home. Willard Richards copied it into the Book of the Law of the Lord that December.
summary: This short revelation addresses Brigham Young as a dear and well-beloved brother. The Lord’s voice tells Brigham he no longer has to leave his family as before. It says his offering is accepted. It says the Lord has seen his labor and travel for His name. Then it gives two commands. Brigham is to send the Lord’s word abroad. He is also to take special care of his family from then on.

contextNote.title: Sending the word without leaving home
contextNote.text: Brigham Young had spent much of the past decade away on missions. Verse 1 says that kind of leaving is “no more required”. The reason given is that his offering is already acceptable. Verse 2 adds that the Lord has seen his “labor and toil in journeyings”. Verse 3 then joins two duties in one command: he must “send my word abroad” and “take especial care of your family”. As President of the Twelve, he could send others out rather than go himself. In this passage, the release from travel is a new assignment, not a retirement.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 125–128 draws from verse 3 that the Lord wants His disciples to care for their families. How does verse 2 describe Brigham’s past years of travel before verse 3 changes his duties?
reviewNote: Read all 3 verses. Official heading gives 9 July 1841 at Brigham Young’s home in Nauvoo, after nearly two years in England. The JSP page loaded did not display its historical introduction, so I read it through the JSP Doctrine and Covenants Study Companion (churchofjesuschrist.org jsp-revelations dc-126): 1 July return with Kimball and Taylor, family hardship, Willard Richards copying it on 17 December 1841, original dictation not located. Kimball, Taylor, and Richards appear only in the setting. Fact-check 2026-10-12: no changes
